procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25M, overdue follow-up (physical last fall never got booked).

Mentions in passing that he was "at the ER for a few hours" around Thanksgiving after "a thing with the cops." Vague on details; says he was checked over and let go and that nothing medical happened. We have no record of it. He agrees to us requesting it.

Otherwise feels fine. Smoking a pack a day. Drinking daily, binges most nights; AUDIT-C 11. Cocaine "here and there." Still on daily aspirin. No GI bleeding symptoms. PHQ-9 3, denies feeling down.

Exam: Vitals as charted. NAD. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen nontender.

A/P
1. ED visit Nov 2022: records request sent to the hospital ED (release signed today).
2. Alcohol / cocaine / tobacco use disorders: unchanged; brief counseling; declines referral and is clear he doesn't want to revisit it every visit.
3. Physical with labs later this year.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request + signed release to the hospital's HIM department for ED record of 11/22-11/23/2022. Confirmation page received. Will scan when it comes in.

documents.title: Records Request Follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No ED record received yet from January request. Called HIM, they have no request on file. Re-faxed request and release, gave direct fax number.

documents.title: Outside Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from 11/23/2022 received by fax (5 pages). Scanned to Media and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside Record Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed the November ED record. Brought in by police for medical evaluation after a car break-in; BAL 0.08%, urine positive for cocaine; no injuries. ED behavioral health clinician documented a long pattern back to childhood (school suspensions for fighting and stealing before 15 per his mother), multiple arrests, and lack of remorse, and gave an impression of antisocial personality disorder. Added to problem list. It fits with how disengaged he is from any talk about the drinking. No medical follow-up needed from the visit itself. Will keep the door open on substance use treatment.

documents.title: Emergency Department Visit Summary
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, ED visit summary to PCP
Date of service: 07/31/2023 22:40 to 08/01/2023 05:15
Patient: Jacob Healey, 25 M. Allergies: NKDA. Meds: aspirin 325 mg daily OTC.

Chief complaint: intoxication; brought in by partner.

HPI: Second visit here this year (previously 11/2022, brought by police). Partner found him at home drunk this evening and was worried because he has a job interview first thing tomorrow. Pt states he finished a full bottle of whiskey over the evening. Explains he wanted to calm his nerves ahead of the interview, that plenty of people drink and he isn't harming anybody, that drinking makes it easier for him to be around people, and that the pressure of looking for work earns him a night off now and then. Does not think his drinking is a problem and believes he could stop if he decided to. No other ingestion reported tonight. Denies SI. No trauma.

PMH: antisocial personality disorder; severe alcohol use disorder; cocaine use disorder; tobacco use (1 ppd x 7 yrs).
FH: father alcohol use disorder (incarcerations); mother MDD and GAD; brother OUD.

Exam: Vital signs within normal limits. Smells of alcohol; intoxicated but alert and redirectable. Otherwise unremarkable: pupils equal and reactive, no head trauma, heart and lungs normal, abdomen soft, moving all extremities.

Course: monitored in the ED, PO fluids, no medications required. Clinically sober and tolerating PO by morning.

Impression: acute alcohol intoxication in a patient with severe alcohol use disorder.
Disposition: discharged home with partner. Substance use treatment resources given. Follow up with PCP.

[Received by fax 08/07/2023]

documents.title: Post-ED Outreach
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP, called re: ED visit 7/31 for intoxication. Pt answered, said he's fine and "it was blown out of proportion." Agreed to a follow-up visit; booked 8/22 at 3:20. Asked about any shakes, sweats or confusion since; denies.

documents.title: Missed Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not come to 8/22 appt. Left voicemail to reschedule. Also sent portal reminder.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26M, finally in after the July ED visit (missed the August appointment).

ED summary reviewed with him: drank a full bottle of whiskey the night before a job interview, partner brought him in, observed overnight and sent home. Frames that night the same way the ED did: he needed to relax, everyone drinks. Still believes he can stop when he wants. Hasn't tried.

Current use: daily, binges 5-6 nights/wk at 10-15 drinks; AUDIT-C 12. Cocaine at parties. Cigarettes 1 ppd, ~7 yrs. Aspirin most mornings. No withdrawal symptoms, no GI bleeding, no chest pain.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Alert, a little irritable with the topic. No tremor, no asterixis. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly.

A/P
1. Acute intoxication (ED 7/31): resolved.
2. Severe alcohol use disorder: I was direct that this was the second ED trip in a year. Offered outpatient program referral and a follow-up just for this; declined both.
3. Cocaine use disorder and nicotine dependence: unchanged, counseled.
4. Antisocial personality disorder: per ED evaluation; no treatment plan, noted.
5. Flu vaccine given.
Physical in spring.
